deals.title: She was free.
deals.description: Yesterday I arrived in Vienna. I got dressed without thinking much about it: white top, black leggings, tall black boots, a cap. 🤍🖤 👉 Then I stepped out of my apartment and saw this drawing in a shop window. A rider of the Spanish Riding School on a white Lipizzaner stallion, rearing in perfect balance. And something in me stopped. I looked just like him. So I went down the rabbit hole. 🐎 The Spanish Riding School was founded in 1565 and is the oldest riding school in the world still in operation. Its riders wear tall black boots, a dark fitted coat and a hat, and they ride pure white horses. Without realizing it, I had dressed as both the rider AND the horse. 👉 For more than 400 years, every rider at the school was a man. The first women were only admitted in 2008. But one woman in this city’s history understood horses as freedom. Empress Sisi married into the strictest court in Europe at 16 and never fit its rules. So she rode. Daily, fearlessly, across the hunting fields of England and Ireland, earning a reputation as one of the finest horsewomen of her time. On horseback, she wasn’t playing a role. She was free. 🤍 Then there’s Alois Podhajsky, the school’s director, who at the end of WWII worked with General Patton to rescue the Lipizzaners and save the breed from disappearing. One man’s devotion to his craft preserved centuries of mastery. Is it an ancestral memory? Another timeline? I don’t know. 💫 But I believe our intuition recognizes things before our mind can explain them. Discipline, grace, mastery, a partnership between strength and gentleness: that’s what I felt looking at that drawing, and it’s what I spend my life helping people find in themselves. Have you ever felt that kind of recognition in a place you’d never been before? Tell me below. 👇 #Vienna #Wien #SpanishRidingSchool #Lipizzaner #EmpressSisi Intuition GeniusZone Mastery Paulina Amador
